cards.front: How do you enable method chaining on a method?
cards.back: Return this from it, so the call yields the same object and another call can follow immediately
cards.extra: public Dialog setTitle(String t) { this.title = t; return this; } — the return value is what makes the next dot possible.
cards.source: stackoverflow.com — How to achieve method chaining in Java?
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::08 Method Chaining

cards.front: What is the Builder pattern's relationship to chaining?
cards.back: The builder's setters return the builder; a final build() returns the finished object
cards.extra: Chaining configures the builder, then one call produces an immutable product — validation happens once, at build time.
cards.source: stackoverflow.com — How to achieve method chaining in Java?
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::08 Method Chaining

cards.front: Why do builders exist when chaining setters already works?
cards.back: They allow final fields and validation before construction — the object is never in a half-configured state
cards.extra: A mutable object built by chained setters is invalid between calls. A builder keeps the mess outside the product.
cards.source: stackoverflow.com — How to achieve method chaining in Java?
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::08 Method Chaining

cards.front: What breaks if you make ordinary JavaBean setters return this?
cards.back: Frameworks that expect void setters — some data mappers and drivers reflectively require the JavaBeans signature
cards.extra: Jackson, for instance, is tolerant, but several persistence libraries are not. Keep void setters and add withX() methods for chaining.
cards.source: stackoverflow.com — How to achieve method chaining in Java?
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::08 Method Chaining

cards.front: Why does chaining break down with inheritance?
cards.back: A method declared to return Base returns a Base reference, so subclass-only methods are no longer callable in the chain
cards.extra: Fixes: covariant return types per class, or the self-type idiom class Builder<B extends Builder> with (B) this.
cards.source: stackoverflow.com — How to achieve method chaining in Java?
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::08 Method Chaining

cards.front: How does Lombok generate chained setters?
cards.back: @Accessors(chain = true) on the class, or lombok.accessors.chain = true project-wide
cards.extra: It generates public Foo setX(T x) { this.x = x; return this; } instead of the void setter.
cards.source: stackoverflow.com — How to achieve method chaining in Java?
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::08 Method Chaining

cards.front: When is chaining the wrong choice?
cards.back: When the methods must return something meaningful, or when callers should not depend on mutation order
cards.extra: A chain reads as a single configured expression. If the calls are actually steps of an algorithm, a chain hides that.
cards.source: stackoverflow.com — How to achieve method chaining in Java?
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::08 Method Chaining

cards.front: What does the fluent API style call this technique?
cards.back: Fluent interface — an API designed so calls read as a sentence: dialog.title("x").message("y").show()
cards.extra: The chaining is the syntax; fluency is the goal. It works best when each step returns the same configured object.
cards.source: stackoverflow.com — How to achieve method chaining in Java?
